name: SOC Platform Compromise
description: An attacker breaches the multi-tenant SIEM and monitoring platform, gaining visibility into client environments, detections, and response playbooks.
threat: Sophisticated intruder targeting the security supply chain
assumptions: Any confirmed platform breach requires notifying every tenant regardless of proven access.
Primary loss covers forensics, per-client investigation support, and rebuild.
Secondary loss covers client attrition and liability claims under service agreements.

name: Remote-Access Tooling Abused Into Clients
description: Attackers compromise the RMM/remote-access tooling used for client response and ride it into customer environments, echoing the MSP supply-chain pattern.
asset: Remote management tooling and standing client access
effect: Client environments compromised through the MSSP
assumptions: Loss scales with the number of clients reachable from the compromised tooling tier.
Primary loss covers incident response across affected clients at the MSSP's cost.
Secondary loss covers contract terminations, litigation, and reputational collapse risk.

name: Analyst Misuses Client Security Data
description: A SOC analyst with broad tenant access exports client vulnerability data and incident histories — a sellable map of every client's weaknesses.
threat: Malicious insider with privileged SOC access
assumptions: Frequency reflects SOC headcount, turnover, and the breadth of standing tenant access.
Primary loss covers investigation and mandatory client disclosure.
Secondary loss covers client losses and claims if exposed weaknesses are exploited.

name: Ransomware on Internal Business Systems
description: Ransomware hits the MSSP's own corporate systems — ticketing, billing, knowledge base — an operational and deeply reputational incident for a security firm.
asset: Internal ticketing, billing, and knowledge systems
assumptions: SOC delivery continues on segregated infrastructure; the loss is corporate-side.
Primary loss covers rebuild and SLA make-goods for delayed deliverables.
Secondary loss is dominated by competitive damage — a breached security vendor loses deals.

name: Client Credential Vault Exposure
description: The vault holding privileged client credentials for managed response is targeted; exposure would hand attackers keys to dozens of environments.
threat: Targeted intrusion against the credential vault
assumptions: Every credential in the vault rotates on suspicion of exposure — cost scales with client count.
Primary loss covers emergency rotation, client coordination, and forensics.
Secondary loss covers liability where rotation lags allow client-side compromise.
